XGBoost permutation sweep — model, split & knob params

2026-06-19

Summary

The reference model is the selected version: an XGBoost classifier with an adaptive train/test split (auto-tuned label-weights + seed search) and a 12-model CV grid for hyperparameters. This report runs a permutation sweep over three parameter families and lets each family “vote” for its best setting, to see whether any combination beats the selected version.

  • Model param — 10 hyperparameter variants (M1–M10), on a fixed split.
  • Split (train/test) param — 10 directed variants (S1–S10) + a 27-cell grid (V1–V27: test-frac × critical-weight × min-count floor).
  • Knob param — 4 data/weighting ablations (A1–A4).

Reading the metrics. Overall Accuracy is dominated by the Tumor majority. The real tuning target is critical-class recall (mean sensitivity over the rare types: MDSC, BnT, Igg, mregDC, PMN_MDSC, Neutrophil) and Kappa. Caveat: the selected version and each split permutation use different held-out sets, so metrics are indicative, not strictly comparable; the selected version’s tiny rare-class test counts (below) inflate its rare-class recall. Only the M1–M10 model-param variants share one fixed split and are mutually comparable.

The selected version reaches critical recall 0.889, Kappa 0.974, balanced accuracy 0.972. But its adaptive split leaves as few as 2 cells for some rare classes in the test set, so several class sensitivities are 1.000 over 2–3 cells — high but high-variance. Its chosen config is a flexible depth-5 tree with no extra regularization; the permutation study below tests whether added regularization and a guaranteed rare-class test floor do better.

Takeaway: on the fixed split, M2 (+max_delta_step) gives the best rare-class recall (0.878 vs M1 baseline 0.764). Deeper/heavily-regularized trees (M5, M8) push overall accuracy up but drop rare recall — the majority-class trap. The selected version’s own number (0.889) sits above the M-grid, but that reflects its depth-5 config and its small rare-class test sample; the same config family without max_delta_step lands near M8 on the fixed split (0.821).

Split (train/test) param permutation

The split changes which images/cells are held out, so accuracy is not comparable; we judge splits by critical-class recall and rare-class coverage (min_test_count_observed — the smallest number of test cells any critical class gets).

Directed sweep (S1–S10)

Full grid (V1–V27): frac × critical-weight × floor

Takeaway: the strongest, most reproducible rare-class recall comes from test-frac 0.20 with a non-trivial floor (≥8) and moderate-to-high critical up-weight (grid cells V5/V8/V7 ≈ 0.82–0.86). A zero floor starves rare classes in the test set, and test-frac 0.40 spreads them too thin — both degrade the estimate. The selected split sits near the good region but with too low a floor.

Knob param permutation (A1–A4)

These change the data or class weights, not the tree hyperparameters (all use the M1 config).

Knob (ablation) variants vs baseline M1
model_id knob Accuracy Kappa BalAcc Crit recall
A1 ablation_capped_weights 0.981 0.934 0.892 0.710
A2 ablation_drop_undefined 0.980 0.927 0.887 0.667
A3 ablation_area_qc 0.986 0.952 0.889 0.676
A4 ablation_outlier_remove 0.984 0.943 0.894 0.671

Takeaway: every knob (capping weights, dropping undefined, area QC, outlier removal) raises Kappa/accuracy but lowers critical recall — they trade rare-class sensitivity for cleaner majority-class fit. None win the vote on the metric that matters here.

Conclusion — what wins the vote

  • Model param: the selected CV grid picks a flexible depth-5 tree with no extra regularization. On a fixed, fairly-sampled split the sweep shows that adding max_delta_step (M2) is what actually lifts rare-class recall (0.878); deeper trees alone (M5/M8) raise accuracy but not rare recall. Vote: add max_delta_step.
  • Split (train/test) param: the selected adaptive split is sound on overall metrics but leaves only 2 test cells for the rarest classes, so its rare-class recall is high-variance. Vote: keep test-frac 0.20 + critical weight 40–100, add a rare-class test floor ≥ 8.
  • Knob param: none improve rare-class recall — they trade it for headline accuracy. Vote: keep the inverse-frequency weighting (undefined/10, Igg/30).

Net: the selected version is strong (Kappa 0.974, balanced accuracy 0.972), but its rare-class evaluation is under-powered. The two upgrades that win the vote are max_delta_step in the model param and a rare-class test-count floor in the split — neither is in the current pipeline.
